% main.tex -- ICSE 2027, Software Engineering in Practice (SEIP) track.
% Build with `make draft` from this directory (see README.md). Sections live
% in sections/, hand-built floats in floats/, tables generated by
% vera-foundry in tables/. apsec/main_apsec.tex is a different paper: no number,
% table or sentence of it may reappear here (`make check` guards this).
\documentclass[10pt,conference]{IEEEtran}
\IEEEoverridecommandlockouts
\input{support/preamble}

% Title options from the roadmap (section 9); to settle with Legal/Risk (decision D22).
\makeatletter
\@namedef{icse@titleA}{Model Review Under the AI Act in a\\ European Bank: One Evaluation Engine,\\ Two Model Families}
\@namedef{icse@titleB}{Fairness Is a Policy Choice:\\ Auditable Model Review Across Machine Learning\\ and Language Models in a European Bank}
\@namedef{icse@titleC}{From Benchmark Scores to Review Decisions:\\ Deploying an Evaluation Engine in a\\ Bank's Model Risk Function}
\newcommand{\icsetitletext}{\def\\{ }\@nameuse{icse@title\icsetitle}}
% \icseinput{file}: every section file, or only \icseonly when the Makefile's
% section target sets it (one section with the full preamble).
\newcommand{\icseinput}[1]{%
  \ifdefined\icseonly\ifdefstring{\icseonly}{#1}{\input{sections/#1}}{}%
  \else\input{sections/#1}\fi}
\makeatother

\begin{document}

\ificsedraft\ifdefined\icseonly\else\input{support/cockpit}\fi\fi

\makeatletter
\title{\@nameuse{icse@title\icsetitle}}
\makeatother

% SEIP reviews are not anonymous, so the paper always builds named. The block
% lives in authors.tex, which is NOT version-controlled (the anonymized
% mirror proxies this repository). It is separate from authors_apsec.tex: the
% two papers do not share an author list.
\author{%
  \InputIfFileExists{authors}{}{%
    \IEEEauthorblockN{Author list withheld}
    \IEEEauthorblockA{authors\_icse.tex is absent from this checkout}%
  }%
}

\maketitle
\icsebodystart

\begin{abstract}
\icseinput{00-abstract}
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
Model risk management, fairness, large language models, evaluation engines, EU AI Act, software engineering in practice
\end{IEEEkeywords}
